newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Deaths likely in Russia apartment block collapse.
newsitem.headline: Deaths likely in Russia apartment block collapse.

text.p: Part of an old five-storey apartment block collapsed in the southern Russian city of Saratov on Monday and it was likely that some people were killed, officials said.
An Emergencies Ministry spokeswoman in Moscow said two people had been rescued alive and taken to hospital but it was not clear how many people might be under the rubble.
"There is a great likelihood that people were killed," the spokeswoman in Moscow.
She later added: "Two people were lucky enough to survive, Thank God."
She said it was not known what caused the collapse but that an explosion had been ruled out.
A local official in Saratov on the Volga river said by telephone that one section of the building had suddenly collapsed at about 11 a.m. (0700 GMT). Deaths were likely, he said.

"Rescue workers have started combing the rubble and are evacuating people living in other sections of the building," said the official, a spokesman at the civil defence headquarters in Saratov, about 750 km (470 miles) southeast of Moscow.
He did not say how many people lived there and did not speculate what had caused the collapse.

"Information on possible victims and reasons for the collapse is being checked out," the spokesman said. Itar-Tass news agency said rescue teams had been rushed to the scene, as well as 10 ambulances.
The Emergencies Ministry said it was also sending a rescue team to Saratov.
